+## #3271 - Site tests skip the generated catalog block before the operation icon
+
+**Decided:** the site tests (`test_guide_icons.py`, `test_guide_refresh.py`)
+read an operation section's lead after one leading, well-formed
+`<!-- catalog:examples:start -->` .. `<!-- catalog:examples:end -->` block
+(`section_lead`). The icon and the toolpath picture must still be the first
+content of the section after that block. The guide pages and the generator
+stay as they are.
+
+**Why:** `cargo xtask catalog` (`xtask/src/catalog_links.rs`, `render`)
+writes the block directly under each operation heading, and
+`cargo xtask catalog --check` fails when the block is not there. To move
+the icon above the block, the generator would have to find and step over
+the icon line, and its check would have to accept prose between the heading
+and the block. That makes the generator read guide prose, which its own
+comment forbids ("never eat guide prose"). With the test change, each check
+keeps one owner: xtask owns the block under the heading, and the site test
+owns the icon as the first line of the section's own content. The helper
+skips one block only, and only with its end marker, so a missing icon, a
+block lower in the section or an unclosed block still fails the icon check.
+
+**Dropped:** move the icon above the block in each section and teach the
+generator to insert the block after the icon line. It changes a process
+file (`xtask/`) and the 44 sections, and it couples the generator to the
+icon shortcode.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low. A different block position needs one change
+in `render` and in `section_lead`, and a `cargo xtask catalog` run.

+## V-Carve
+
+<!-- catalog:examples:start -->
+**Example cases**
+
+No catalog case yet.
+<!-- catalog:examples:end -->
+
+{{ <icon name="op-v-carve" /> }} ![Top view of the V-bit tip following the centre line of a picked outline.](../../../operation-paths.svg#VCarve)
+
+**For:** carving letters, logos and other closed shapes with the cone of a
+V-bit. The tip follows the centre line of each picked outline and goes as
+deep as the shape is wide at that place, so the cone touches the two walls
+together. Choose it over Engrave when the shape has width, not only a
+stroke.
+
+**Tool:** a chamfer mill (V-bit). Its tip angle sets the cone, and its
+flute must cover the deepest cut.
+
+**Picks:** closed outlines. The V-bit cuts inside them.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Top Z | the model top (the start depth) |
+| Heights | Bottom Z | 2 under Top Z (the maximum depth of the tip) |
+| Heights | Stepdown | the document stepdown |
+| Passes | Flat clearing | off |
+| Passes | Floor stepover | 0.25 (shown only with flat clearing on) |
+
+Where the shape is wider than the cone at the maximum depth, the tip stops
+at Bottom Z. Flat clearing then cuts that floor flat at the floor
+stepover; with it off, the wide places keep the material that the cone
+does not reach.
+
+**Common refusals:** "V-Carve cuts with the cone of a V-bit - it needs a
+chamfer mill (V-bit)"; "the cone of ... has ... mm of flute, short of the
+... mm maximum depth of this V-Carve"; "V-Carve needs Top of Part Z: set
+the height".
+

+CATALOG_START = "<!-- catalog:examples:start -->"
+CATALOG_END = "<!-- catalog:examples:end -->"
+
+
+def section_lead(body):
+    """Return a section body after its generated catalog block (#3271).
+
+    `cargo xtask catalog` writes the example-case block directly under each
+    operation heading, and `cargo xtask catalog --check` holds it there. The
+    section's own content starts after that block. Only one leading,
+    well-formed block is skipped: a block elsewhere or without its end
+    marker leaves the body as it is, so the icon check still fails.
+    """
+    body = body.lstrip()
+    if body.startswith(CATALOG_START + "\n"):
+        end = body.find("\n" + CATALOG_END + "\n")
+        if end != -1:
+            body = body[end + len(CATALOG_END) + 2:].lstrip()
+    return body
+
+
